payload.claim: Revisit at the FY2026 annual report and the Q1 2027 report. The case improves if a major new Transmission award stops the backlog decline from EUR 12.4bn, FCF turns positive as Karlskrona, Cologne and the second vessel come online on schedule in 2027, and 2027 guidance supports the roughly EUR 570m EBITDA consensus. It weakens if any of the 2027 capacity additions is delayed, 2027 EBITDA guidance comes in clearly below consensus, net cash keeps falling while organic growth stays negative, the Transmission margin uplift from post-2023 contracts fails to appear, or the integrity gate escalates beyond Flag (for example, cartel findings that reach the HV business or a large undisclosed provision). A material widening of the margin of safety at the 7% rate on unchanged assumptions would also prompt a re-rating of the verdict.

prediction.reasoning: Organic growth is -7% year to date, Q1-Q3 standard-metal revenue is EUR 1,940m against 2,079m, Q3 missed consensus on revenue, and the new capacity only arrives in 2027. FY2026 revenue growth should therefore fall well short of the 7.5%/yr the reverse DCF assumes, even after metal-price pass-through lifts reported revenue.
